name: Cypress Test Automation
certifications: No official Cypress certification; assessed by capstone projects
ISTQB Advanced Level Test Automation Engineering (CTAL-TAE)

beginner.summary: For manual testers and front-end developers starting test automation with Cypress. Covers installing Cypress, JavaScript for testers, writing specs, selecting elements, interacting with pages, assertions, retry-ability, fixtures, custom commands, cy.intercept, forms, iframes and new tabs, cy.session, cy.request, configuration and environments, screenshots and videos, headless and CI runs, page objects or app actions, and debugging.
prerequisites: Knows how to test a web application by hand
Can use a terminal and install Node.js
outcomes: Write readable Cypress tests that use retry-ability instead of fixed waits
Stub network calls and prepare state with cy.request and cy.session
Organise suites with fixtures, custom commands and environments
Run Cypress headless in CI and debug failures with the command log, screenshots and videos

days.topic: Cypress Overview, Installation and Project Setup
subtopics: What Cypress is and how it runs inside the browser
Cypress compared with Selenium and Playwright
Supported browsers: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Electron
The launchpad and choosing end-to-end or component testing
The generated folders and cypress.config file
The command log and time travel
Example specs and how to remove them
days.lab_task: Install Cypress in a sample front-end project, run the example specs in the interactive runner and headless in two browsers, and explore the command log.
days.deliverable: Working Cypress project with first runs
checks: Cypress opens and lists the example specs
cypress run passes in two browsers
A snapshot of an earlier command is inspected

days.topic: JavaScript Essentials for Cypress Testers
subtopics: Callbacks and why Cypress commands are not promises
then and wrap for working with yielded values
Common JavaScript mistakes in Cypress code
days.lab_task: Write helper functions for test data in a module, use .then to work with a yielded value, and fix three examples where a developer treated Cypress commands like promises.
days.deliverable: Helper module and fixed examples
checks: Helpers are imported and used in a spec
Values are read with .then or aliases, not return values

days.topic: Writing Tests with describe, it and Hooks
subtopics: Spec files and the Mocha structure
days.lab_task: Write a spec with five tests for a sample web shop using describe blocks and hooks, run only one test with .only and read a deliberately failing test's message.
days.deliverable: Spec with five passing tests
checks: Five tests pass in the runner
The failing test's cause is noted from its message

days.topic: Selecting Elements: Selectors, data-cy and Best Practices
subtopics: find, within and eq for scoping
days.lab_task: Replace ten brittle selectors in an old suite with data-cy attributes or text-based selectors, scope table checks with within, and agree attribute naming with a developer.
days.deliverable: Rewritten selectors and naming agreement
checks: At least eight selectors use data-cy or text
Table checks are scoped with within
Developers accept the attribute naming rule

days.topic: Interacting with Elements: Click, Type, Check and Select
subtopics: Why force: true hides real problems
days.lab_task: Automate a registration form with text fields, dropdowns, checkboxes, radio buttons and a file upload, submit it and check the confirmation page.
days.deliverable: Automated form spec
checks: All field types are filled with Cypress commands
The uploaded file name appears on the confirmation page

days.topic: Assertions with should and expect
days.lab_task: Add assertions to the web shop spec for visibility, text, counts, URLs and classes, and rewrite two negative assertions that passed for the wrong reason.
days.deliverable: Spec with complete assertions
checks: Each test asserts a visible outcome
Both negative assertions fail when the bug is reintroduced
One complex check uses a should callback

days.topic: Retry-Ability and How Cypress Waits
subtopics: Why cy.wait with a number is a smell
Writing tests that are stable by design
days.lab_task: Remove every fixed cy.wait from a flaky spec using retry-able queries and aliased requests, then run the spec twenty times to confirm it is stable.
days.deliverable: Stable spec with no fixed waits
checks: No cy.wait with a number remains
The spec passes twenty runs in a row
Notes explain which commands retry and which do not

days.topic: Fixtures and Test Data
subtopics: Generating data with libraries such as Faker

days.deliverable: Fixture files and data-driven tests
checks: Tests load data from fixture files
Each run uses unique sign-up data
Created users are deleted after tests

days.topic: Custom Commands
subtopics: When to write a custom command
Typing custom commands for editor help
days.lab_task: Write custom commands for login, adding a product to the cart and checking a toast message, use them across three specs and document them.
days.deliverable: Command file and refactored specs
checks: Three commands are defined and used
Repeated steps across specs are replaced by commands

days.topic: Network Stubbing with cy.intercept
subtopics: Matching by method, URL and query
When to stub and when to hit the real back end

days.deliverable: Network stubbing specs with a stubbing policy
checks: Empty, error and slow cases are tested
The form's request body is checked

days.topic: Testing Forms and Validation
days.lab_task: Test a multi-step form's validation for required fields, formats and boundaries with data-driven tests, including a server-side validation error stubbed with cy.intercept.
days.deliverable: Form validation spec
checks: Required, format and boundary rules are tested
A stubbed server validation error is shown to the user
Validation cases come from a data list

days.topic: Handling Iframes, New Tabs and Alerts in Cypress
subtopics: Testing the link target instead of switching tabs

days.deliverable: Spec covering iframes, tabs and dialogs
checks: Fields inside the iframe are filled and checked
The new-tab link is checked through its target and URL
Confirm and prompt behaviours are tested

days.topic: Sessions and Login with cy.session
subtopics: Why logging in through the UI each time is slow

days.deliverable: Session-based login with timing comparison
checks: Login runs once per user per run
Expired sessions are detected and recreated
Suite time drops after the change

days.topic: API Requests with cy.request
subtopics: cy.request for GET, POST, PUT and DELETE
days.lab_task: Write API specs for create, read, update and delete of products, then use cy.request to prepare data for a UI test and remove it afterwards.
days.deliverable: API specs and an API-backed UI test
checks: All four operations have status and body checks
The UI test uses data created with cy.request
Created products are deleted after the test

days.topic: Cypress Configuration and Environments
subtopics: Overriding config from the command line
days.lab_task: Configure the suite for local, test and staging environments with environment variables, set retries for run mode only and run the suite against two environments.
days.deliverable: Environment-aware configuration
checks: The same suite runs against two environments
No credentials are stored in config files
Retries apply in run mode only

days.topic: Screenshots, Videos and the Command Log
subtopics: Reading the command log after a failure
days.lab_task: Enable videos for failed specs, take evidence screenshots in a checkout test, add a JUnit reporter and share one failure with a developer using the artefacts.
days.deliverable: Configured artefacts and a shared failure report
checks: Failed specs have screenshots and videos
The developer can reproduce the failure from the evidence

days.topic: Running Cypress Headless and in CI
subtopics: Uploading screenshots and videos as artefacts

days.deliverable: Working CI workflow
checks: The workflow runs on a pull request
Tests run only after the app is ready

days.topic: Page Objects or App Actions in Cypress
subtopics: App actions through the application's own code
Choosing an approach as a team
days.lab_task: Implement the same checkout test three ways (page objects, custom commands and app actions), compare readability and maintenance and choose an approach for the team.
days.deliverable: Three implementations and a team decision
checks: A comparison table covers readability and maintenance

days.topic: Debugging Cypress Tests
subtopics: Browser developer tools during a run
Debugging in run mode with logs
Common errors: detached elements, timeouts and cross-origin
days.lab_task: Diagnose three broken specs (a timeout, a detached element and a cross-origin error) using the command log, cy.pause and developer tools, and write a debugging checklist.
days.deliverable: Diagnosis notes, fixes and a checklist
checks: Each failure has a recorded cause
All three specs pass after the fixes

days.topic: Beginner Capstone: Cypress Test Suite for a Single-Page App
days.lab_task: Build a Cypress suite for a single-page web shop covering search, cart, checkout and account with data-cy selectors, custom commands, cy.session, stubbed error cases and a CI workflow with artefacts.
days.deliverable: Complete Cypress suite with CI
checks: Each critical journey has passing tests
Commands, fixtures and sessions are used consistently
The suite runs on pull requests with artefacts

intermediate.summary: For testers and developers who write Cypress tests and now build a team framework. Covers component testing, TypeScript, test architecture with tasks and plugins, cross-origin testing, Cypress Cloud parallelisation and recording, flaky test detection and Test Replay, visual regression, accessibility, database seeding with cy.task, mocking time and browser APIs, BDD with Cucumber, code coverage, testing GraphQL and REST back ends, multi-environment pipelines, reporting, files, SSO flows, Docker and Cypress's known limits.
prerequisites: Writes Cypress tests with selectors, intercepts and custom commands
Comfortable with JavaScript or TypeScript and Git
outcomes: Build a Cypress framework with end-to-end and component tests
Run suites in parallel with Cypress Cloud and control flakiness
Add visual, accessibility and BDD tests where they add value
Handle complex flows such as cross-origin logins, files and seeded data

days.topic: Component Testing with Cypress for React and Vue
subtopics: Stubbing child components and network calls
Styling and providers in component tests
Component tests compared with end-to-end tests

days.deliverable: Component test specs in CI
checks: Three components are mounted and tested
Component and end-to-end specs both run in the pipeline

days.topic: Cypress with TypeScript
subtopics: Linting and type checking in CI

checks: Specs, support files and fixtures follow the layout
A colleague adds a passing spec using the guide

Avoiding cross-origin steps with API login
days.lab_task: Automate a login that redirects to a test identity provider with cy.origin, pass credentials safely, then add an API-based login and compare both approaches.
days.deliverable: Cross-origin login test and comparison
checks: The redirect login completes in the test
Credentials are passed with the args option
Speed and stability of both logins are compared
objectives: Choose between UI and API login

days.topic: Parallelisation and Recording with Cypress Cloud
subtopics: Grouping runs by browser or type
Alternatives when Cloud is not available
days.lab_task: Record runs to Cypress Cloud, run the suite in parallel on four CI machines, group runs by browser and compare total time with a single machine.
days.deliverable: Parallel recorded pipeline with timing comparison

days.deliverable: Flake report, fixes and policy

subtopics: Tasks that call the database or seed scripts
Per-test data compared with per-suite data
Seeding through APIs instead of the database

days.deliverable: Seeding tasks and specs

days.topic: Mocking Time, Geolocation and Browser APIs

checks: The timeout test runs without real waiting

days.topic: BDD with the Cypress Cucumber Preprocessor

checks: Scenarios are reviewed by a business stakeholder

subtopics: What coverage tells and does not tell

days.deliverable: Coverage report and new tests
checks: A combined coverage report is produced
One redundant test is removed with a reason

subtopics: REST and GraphQL in the same app
Keeping stubs close to the schema

days.deliverable: GraphQL stubbing specs
checks: Each operation is aliased by its name
Error and empty results are shown correctly

Running against test and staging environments

Each stage targets the right environment with its secrets

The PDF contains the order number and total

days.topic: Authentication Flows: SSO, OAuth and Tokens

days.topic: Cypress and Docker

days.deliverable: Docker Compose setup and container pipeline

The container-only failure has a recorded cause and fix

days.topic: Cypress Limitations and Workarounds

days.deliverable: Limits list, workarounds and a tool decision
checks: Each limit is linked to a product scenario

days.topic: Intermediate Capstone: Component and End-to-End Suite with Cypress Cloud
days.lab_task: Build a TypeScript Cypress framework with component and end-to-end tests, seeded data, programmatic login, accessibility and visual checks and parallel recorded runs, and hand it to a colleague to extend.
days.deliverable: Team framework, pipeline and handover notes
checks: Component and end-to-end suites both pass
Recorded parallel runs meet the time target
A colleague adds a spec without help

advanced.summary: For automation leads, SDETs and front-end quality engineers who run Cypress for several teams. Covers Cypress at scale in monorepos, writing plugins, large-suite performance, advanced network control and contract checks, micro-frontends, security checks, AI-assisted test creation, data strategy, Cloud coverage and accessibility insights, ephemeral environments, migration between Cypress and Playwright, real-time apps, governance, quality gates, feature flags, design systems, CI cost, a centre of excellence and troubleshooting.
prerequisites: Has built and maintained a Cypress framework used by a team
Strong JavaScript or TypeScript and CI skills
Understands test strategy and the test pyramid
outcomes: Run Cypress across many teams and repositories with shared code
Keep large suites fast, stable and cost-effective
Extend Cypress with plugins and connect it to quality gates
Lead tool strategy, governance and migrations for front-end testing

days.topic: Cypress at Scale: Monorepos and Shared Test Libraries

days.lab_task: Move three teams' suites into a monorepo with a shared commands package, run only affected projects on pull requests and upgrade Cypress for one team without breaking others.
days.deliverable: Monorepo layout, shared package and upgrade record
checks: All teams use the shared package

One team's upgrade leaves the others passing

days.topic: Writing Cypress Plugins and Custom Tasks

days.topic: Performance of Large Cypress Suites

days.deliverable: Performance analysis and optimised pipeline
checks: The slowest specs and causes are listed

CI cost per run is compared before and after

Data isolation per run and per team

days.deliverable: Data strategy and failure comparison

days.deliverable: Insight review, new tests and a progress report

days.lab_task: Run Cypress against a preview environment for each pull request with readiness checks and seeded data, and remove the environment after the run.

Running both tools side by side
Choosing which tests to move first

The recommendation states which tool to keep and why
